action_taken: the motor was found getting stuck which was identified as the cause of rate error. then, the motor was lubricated and tested using ida. for 150ml/hr and 10ml vtbi set in the infusion pump,the actual values displayed by ida are: average flow rate: 93.27ml/hr instantenous flow rate: 100.48ml/hr deviation percentage:-37.82 volume infused: 6.36ml the volume infused in the infusion pump was displayed to be 10ml while the actual volume infused was 6.36ml. the deviation percentage at 50ml/hr for 10ml vtbi was found to be -38.02 and at 500ml/hr was found to be -25.03 . hence,the infusion pump can no longer be used.

fault_description: the patient monitor was continuously alarming even when all measured values were within the normal range.

fault_description: the samsung hs70a usg machine was reported to have a printing issue. specifically, the device was unable to print patient records and examination results as required during routine operation.
action_taken: the machine was tested and it was observed that the printer was not receiving any signal from the usg machine. visual inspection of the connections revealed that the cable connecting the printer to the usg machine was not properly secured. the printer cable was reconnected securely to both the printer and the usg machine. after reconnection, the machine was tested again. the printer began to print examination results; however, patient records were still not being printed. a thorough assessment of the usg machine s print settings was conducted. it was discovered that the print option for patient records was set to off in the device settings. the print option was switched to on to enable patient record printing. after this adjustment, the machine was able to print patient records. however, the output was not in the desired format the font size was too small and the color format differed from the standard used in the department. the patient record print setup was accessed and modified. the font size was increased for better readability, and the color format was adjusted to match the department s standard and the doctor s preferences. several test prints were performed to ensure the output met all requirements. now, the machine is fully functional.

fault_description: the ecg machine was reported as non-functional
action_taken: the machine was tested and it was observed that the v2 and v3 signals were not being displayed. the connector was inspected and found to be properly connected; however, the issue persisted. during comprehensive testing, it was noted that pressing the connector caused the signals to appear intermittently. further investigation revealed that pins 7 and 8 of the machine s connector port were discontinuous. the connector was carefully examined, and continuity was restored by soldering the affected pins. testing was performed without reassembling the machine, and the signals were displayed correctly. after reassembling and securing the screws, the problem reoccurred. the connector board was then realigned to ensure that the connector pins did not come into contact with the housing. following this adjustment, the device was tested again and found to be fully functional.

fault_description: the humaclot junior analyzer was reported as non-functional, specifically displaying consistently low prothrombin time (pt) values.
action_taken: upon inspection, it was observed that the analyzer consistently displayed abnormally low pt values across multiple patient samples. to isolate the cause, several samples were tested, all yielding similarly low results, indicating the issue was likely with the analyzer rather than the samples. the following steps were taken: - reagent quality check: verified that the pt reagent used was within the expiry date and properly stored. - temperature verification: confirmed that the incubation chamber maintained a stable temperature of 37 c. - initial cleaning: the optic channel was cleaned due to the presence of visible dirt; however, the problem persisted. - further internal inspection: the device was carefully disassembled. the internal optical channel and detector unit were found to be heavily contaminated with dust particles. - component cleaning and reset: the detector unit and optic components were thoroughly cleaned, and all relevant internal connections were inspected and reset. following reassembly, repeated tests were performed using both the same and multiple fresh samples. the pt results were now within acceptable and varied ranges, consistent with expected values and confirmed by laboratory technicians. now, the machine is fully functional.

action_taken: an oxygen concentrator that had been kept in the store for a long period was brought out for testing in the hope that it would be in usable condition. during the test run, it was found that the unit was delivering a lower flow than the set value for example, when set at 10 lpm, it was delivering only about 7 lpm or less, with an oxygen concentration of 60 to 70 at that flow rate. a thorough inspection was performed. it was initially suspected that the ultrasonic oxygen sensor (us1010) inside the concentrator was not functioning correctly due to extended storage conditions. the sensor was found to be damaged and was replaced with a new unit. after replacing the sensor, the output readings were still inconsistent. to cross-check, the flow meter was replaced with a new unit, which provided improved and more stable readings. this replacement helped restore the correct flow rate. additionally, all internal oxygen delivery pipes were checked, tightened, and re-secured to eliminate any possible leaks or pressure loss. after all parts were serviced and replaced as needed, the oxygen concentrator was tested again and verified to deliver flow rates much closer to the set values.

action_taken: the anesthesia machine was thoroughly inspected following a report of elevated ppeak. ventilator parameters were reviewed and found to be set at a tidal volume of 400 ml with peep of 5-6 cmh₂o. during assessment, the ppeak was observed to be above 28 cmh₂o, while the plateau pressure (pplat) remained stable at 22 23 cmh₂o. the stable pplat indicated that lung compliance was acceptable and that the elevated ppeak was most likely due to increased airway resistance. the patient breathing circuit was inspected and found to be properly connected, unobstructed, and free of condensation. further evaluation of the patient airway revealed that the endotracheal (et) tube was partially obstructed with secretions, causing increased resistance to airflow and resulting in elevated ppeak. the et tube was suctioned and cleared of secretions. following this intervention, the ppeak returned to normal range, confirming that the cause of the issue was airway obstruction rather than a fault in the anesthesia machine.

fault_description: fhr not being detected and printout was faint and intermittent
action_taken: upon inspection, the ultrasound (usg) probe was found to be properly connected to the device and in correct contact with the patient; however, no fhr signal was being detected by the machine. further examination of the probe connector revealed that two pins inside the connector had been pushed down, resulting in poor electrical contact and signal transmission failure. the affected pins were carefully realigned to their correct position. after this correction, the fhr signal was successfully detected and displayed on the monitor. additionally, the printed output was observed to be very faint and inconsistent. the recording paper was checked and found to be in good condition. the thermal print head and roller were then cleaned and properly aligned. during further inspection, it was noted that the locking mechanism securing the roller and maintaining contact between the thermal head and the paper was bent, causing insufficient pressure and poor print quality. the lock was realigned and repositioned to ensure proper contact. following this adjustment, the print quality improved significantly. fhr detection and printing functions were restored, and the ctg machine was confirmed to be operating normally.

fault_description: the device was reported as displaying consistently low prothrombin time (pt) values.
action_taken: upon inspection, it was observed that the analyzer consistently displayed abnormally low pt values across multiple patient samples. to isolate the cause, several samples were tested, all yielding similarly low results, indicating the issue was likely with the analyzer rather than the samples. the following steps were taken: - reagent quality check: verified that the pt reagent used was within the expiry date and properly stored. - temperature verification: confirmed that the incubation chamber maintained a stable temperature of 37 c. - initial cleaning: the optic channel was cleaned due to the presence of visible dirt; however, the problem persisted. - further internal inspection: the device was carefully disassembled. the internal optical channel and detector unit were found to be heavily contaminated with dust particles. - component cleaning and reset: the detector unit and optic components were thoroughly cleaned, and all relevant internal connections were inspected and reset. following reassembly, repeated tests were performed using both the same and multiple fresh samples. the pt results were now within acceptable and varied ranges, consistent with expected values and confirmed by laboratory technicians. now, the machine is fully functional.

fault_description: the unit failed the mandatory t1 (test 1) self-test prior to patient treatment.
action_taken: upon inspection, the t1 test failed and showed error for conductivity. the test was performed multiple times but still it failed. the conductivity value was observed be stay just in between 8 and 9, which indicated that part b pumping had been off. the repair commenced with a hydraulic inspection, where the expired bicarbonate solution ( 24 hours) was replaced with a fresh batch to correct the chemical baseline. to address the instability, a manual syringe priming technique was utilized to clear air pockets and dislodge minor obstructions within the part b intake line. upon finding the suction pipe filter missing, the part b solenoid valve was disassembled and cleaned to remove crystalline buildup, ensuring precise dosing. finally, a new inline filter was installed to prevent future debris ingress. following these interventions, the t1 self-test passed successfully, conductivity stabilized, and the machine exited bypass mode, returning to full operational status.

fault_description: unusual noise and excessive vibration during the initial operation phase
action_taken: upon inspection, the device was observed to vibrate and produce loud mechanical noise shortly after startup. the display triggered a low water level alarm, which automatically activated the water pump; however, a visual check confirmed that the reservoir already contained sufficient water. this false sensor reading caused the pump to overfill the system, forcing water into the steam delivery pipes and potentially reaching the jacket and chamber. to rectify this, the machine was powered down and excess water was manually drained to the appropriate level. a detailed examination of the electronics revealed that the water level sensor cable had become loose, leading to an intermittent signal failure that misled the control board. once the sensor cable was properly tightened and secured, the false alarms ceased, the automatic filling sequence stabilized, and the autoclave returned to normal, quiet operation.

fault_description: the user reported that the screening image was not clear, showing heavy artifacts and static noise on the display. additionally, the screen would intermittently go blank (automatically turn off), and at one point, the system was exposing x-rays, but no image was being rendered on the monitor.
action_taken: connection inspection: conducted a thorough check of all data transmission and video cables. identified a loose connection between the image processor and the display monitor. hardware fix: secured and re-seated all loose connectors and verified cable integrity to eliminate the signal noise and artifacts. system configuration parameter calibration: addressed the issue where the x-ray was exposing without a display output. investigated the system software/firmware settings and found a mismatch in the imaging parameters. parameter adjustment: reset and corrected the digital imaging parameters and memory settings to ensure the captured x-ray signal is correctly processed and routed to the display monitors. functionality test: performed multiple test exposures. verified that the last image hold (lih) function is working correctly and that the display remains stable without turning off or flickering. conclusion: the signal artifacts were successfully resolved by securing the internal connections. the imaging software parameters were re-calibrated to restore the live feed to the display. the system is now fully functional.

fault_description: the user reported a malfunction in the pneumatic control system.
action_taken: system diagnostics: performed a full power-on self-test (post) to check for electronic errors and sensor calibration. observed the low battery indicator and verified power supply stability. internal inspection: opened the chassis to inspect the pneumatic circuit, including the solenoid valves, air pumps, and pressure transducers. checked for any kinks in the internal tubing or loose wire harnesses. valve troubleshooting: identified a logic hang-up in the solenoid valve control. system reset re-calibration: performed a hard reset of all operational parameters and timing sequences (pr, dl, and on settings). this cleared the software-level block affecting the valve actuation. pressure testing: tested both cuff 1 (proximal) and cuff 2 (distal) channels. verified that the unit reaches the set pressure (e.g., 350 mm/hg and holds it without leakage, and that the deflate command triggers the valves immediately.

fault_description: the device was not able to inflate both the proximal and distal cuff

fault_description: fetal heart rate (fhr) was not being detected, and the printout was faint and intermittent.
action_taken: upon inspection, the ultrasound (usg) probe was found to be properly connected to the device and in correct contact with the patient; however, no fhr signal was being detected by the machine. further examination of the probe connector revealed that two pins inside the connector had been pushed down, resulting in poor electrical contact and signal transmission failure. the affected pins were carefully realigned to their correct position. after this correction, the fhr signal was successfully detected and displayed on the monitor. additionally, the printed output was observed to be very faint and inconsistent. the recording paper was checked and found to be in good condition. the thermal print head and roller were then cleaned and properly aligned. during further inspection, it was noted that the locking mechanism securing the roller and maintaining contact between the thermal head and the paper was bent, causing insufficient pressure and poor print quality. the lock was realigned and repositioned to ensure proper contact. following this adjustment, the print quality improved significantly. fhr detection and printing functions were restored, and the ctg machine was confirmed to be operating normally.

fault_description: unusual noise and excessive vibration during the initial operation phase.
action_taken: upon inspection, the device was observed to vibrate and produce loud mechanical noise shortly after startup. the display triggered a low water level alarm, which automatically activated the water pump; however, a visual check confirmed that the reservoir already contained sufficient water. this false sensor reading caused the pump to overfill the system, forcing water into the steam delivery pipes and potentially reaching the jacket and chamber. to rectify this, the machine was powered down and excess water was manually drained to the appropriate level. a detailed examination of the electronics revealed that the water level sensor cable had become loose, leading to an intermittent signal failure that misled the control board. once the sensor cable was properly tightened and secured, the false alarms ceased, the automatic filling sequence stabilized, and the autoclave returned to normal, quiet operation.

fault_description: the bipolar function of the covidien force fx was completely non-functional .
action_taken: upon physical inspection and diagnostic testing, the device was assesed to determine why the foot switch was failing to trigger the bipolar function. it was verified as the primary source of the problem, as the device itself passed self-test protocols. detailed inspection of the foot switch cable assembly revealed that the live wire and the neutral wire on the connector side had become detached from their solder points. to rectify this, both wires were properly resoldered to their respective terminals to ensure a stable electrical connection. additionally, the internal limit switch was checked for mechanical wear and electrical continuity, where it was verified to be fully functional. following the repair, the foot switch was retested with the unit, confirming that the bipolar functionality has been fully restored and is now safe for clinical use.

fault_description: the unit was flagged for consistently high peak inspiratory pressure and a failure to complete the monthly o2 sensor calibration.
action_taken: upon inspection, the ventilator was delivering a 400 ml tidal volume with a peep of 5 6 cmh_2o. clinical observation showed an elevated ppeak exceeding 28 cmh2o, while the plateau pressure remained stable at 22 23 cmh2o. this pressure gradient indicated that the issue was rooted in increased airway resistance rather than a change in patient lung compliance. further investigation revealed that the soda lime was expired, leading to excessive moisture buildup in the breathing circuit that obstructed airflow. simultaneously, the o2 sensor calibration failure was traced to an improperly seated sensor and connector. to rectify these issues, the expired soda lime was replaced, the flow sensors were dried, and the o2 sensor was securely reconnected. following these actions, the o2 calibration passed successfully and ppeak returned to normal parameters, confirming the machine s pneumatic and electronic systems are fully functional.

fault_description: one dome of the ot light was flickering when moved
action_taken: initial inspection revealed that one dome was operating normally but when moved the light flickered. further examination of the hinge/bending section showed a discontinuty indicating an interruption in the power supply path. the power board was tested in coordination with the vendor and was found to be functioning within normal limits. upon detailed inspection, melted rubber insulation was observed on the brass rings of the slip ring assembly. this melted insulation was obstructing proper contact with the carbon/metal brush, resulting in loss of electrical continuity. the melted insulation was removed, the slip ring contacts were cleaned, and the assembly was reassembled; however, the issue persisted. subsequently, the slip ring assembly was replaced, after which continuity was restored and the ot light functioned normally.

fault_description: the cuff was not inflating or deflating during operation.
action_taken: a through inspection of the system was performed to identify the cause of the malfunction. the electrical connections of the inflation motor and solenoid valve were examined, as these components are responsible for cuff inflation and controlled air release. during inspection, it was found that the inflation motor wires were not properly connected, preventing the motor from operating and generating the required air pressure for cuff inflation. the motor wires were therefore reconnected and properly soldered to restore a stable electrical connection. subsequently, the solenoid valve power connection was checked. it was observed that the power supply to the solenoid valve was fluctuating due to a disjoint cold solder joint on the PCB, which resulted in intermittent operation of the valve and affected the deflation mechanism. the defective solder joint was resoldered to ensure a stable and reliable electrical connection. further inspection of the PCB power connections revealed that the voltage was not reaching certain components due to a loose and poor connection in the power line. the power wire was therefore reconnected and properly soldered to the PCB to ensure correct voltage supply. after completing all repairs and reconnections, the system was tested for proper functionality. the cuff inflation and deflation operated normally, confirming that the issue had been resolved. equipment tested and found to be operating normally.

action_taken: verified the input ac voltage supply at the control box using a multimeter. the measured voltage was within the acceptable operating range for the unit. opened the control box and inspected the internal boards. confirmed that the power supply board was functioning correctly and delivering the required 32 v dc output. observed that the driver board was not receiving power from the power supply board. inspected the connecting pins between the power supply board and the driver board. a loose or poor connection was identified. properly re-secured and fixed the connection between the two boards. after the repair, the driver board received proper 32 v dc supply. the green power led on the driver board illuminated, and the medical bed started functioning normally.

fault_description: eeg system s x-keys mwii controller failing to provide prompts
action_taken: upon inspection, the power indicator was glowing but failing to provide prompts. the device was disassambled to inspect the internal circuitry and wiring. all internal wires were found to be continuous and switches were checked and found to be be functioning correctly when the buttons were pressed. the pc also recognised the device connection. despite the harware functionality, the eeg software remained unresponsive. dignosis confirmed that the x-keys internal configuration profiles were corrupted or cleared, resulting in blank or unassigned key mappings within the controller s onboard memory. because the controller was not broadcasting the expected hid key codes, the eeg software could ot register the inputs. a reset of the x-keys controller was performed to clear any transient firmware errors and the xkeys reconfiguration was performed by accessing the x-keys configuration utility to re-map the specific trigger functions required by the eec software to each physical key. following the reassignment of key functions and saving the profile to the device s internal memory, the keyboard was tested against the eec software. the keyboard successfully communicated with the software and prompt/event marking functionality was restored.

action_taken: upon physical inspection, the internal ribbon cable connecting the main circuit boards was loosely seated. this caused the intermittent signal broadcasting. the connection was properly reseated. poat repair, the hotspot was detected and successfully connected via the laptop, with full functionality confirmed in the software but this was still not possible in the mobile devices. a review of the software application revealed that the wireless channel settings were misconfigured. by manually cycling through available frequency channels, a compatible channels was identified. this allowed the android application to successfully establish a connection and display real time utrasound images.

action_taken: the imaging software was experiencing a discrepancy where the live video feed was visible, but captured images resulted in a black frame, indicating that the capture engine was failing to read data from the camera sensor. upon inspection, it was determined that the software s camera frame configuration was undefined, causing the image acquisition path to reference invalid coordinates instead of the active sensor area. this issue was resolved by accessing the set camera utility to properly define and map the active frame area (region of interest) within the software. following this configuration, the acquisition path successfully synchronized with the camera s sensor output, and subsequent testing confirmed that images were being captured correctly and matched the live preview feed.

fault_description: abnormal ecg waveform color lead iii displayed yellow while others remained green.

fault_description: false v-tach (ventricular tachycardia) readings for ecg parameter.
action_taken: the patient monitor was flagged due to displaying anomalous ecg readings, specifically indicating ventricular tachycardia (v-tach) despite the heart rate shown on the display was in the normal range . this discrepancy between the visually stable heart rate and the v-tach alarm suggested a potential issue with the ecg signal acquisition or processing within the monitor. to isolate the source of the problem, the ecg probe connected to the affected monitor was replaced with a probe from a known functional patient monitor. despite the probe exchange, the monitor continued to display the false v-tach waveforms and readings, confirming that the issue was inherent to the patient monitor itself and not due to a faulty ecg probe. he patient monitor was then opened for internal inspection. it was observed that several wires connected to the ecg processing unit appeared to be loose or partially disconnected. these loose connections were identified as the probable cause of the erratic and incorrect ecg waveform interpretation. all identified loose wires related to the ecg circuitry were securely reconnected. following the re-establishment of stable connections, the patient monitor was powered on and thoroughly tested. the ecg waveform now displayed accurate ecg parameter as observed, indicating a more stable interpretation of the cardiac rhythm. the heart rate readings also appeared consistent with the observed rhythm, and the false v-tach alarms ceased. conclusion: the patient monitor is now functional with accurate ecg parameter readings. the issue of false v-tach indications was caused by loose internal wiring affecting the ecg signal processing. the repair, involving the re-connection of these wires, has resolved the problem, and the monitor is now providing reliable ecg data.

fault_description: abnormal ecg waveform color lead iii displayed in yellow, while all other leads appeared in green.

fault_description: collimator light not turning on and magnetic locking system failure.
action_taken: upon inspection, it was found that one of the internal fuses of the generator had blown. a detailed assessment revealed that the cable supplying power to the magnetic locking mechanism had become disconnected from its connector. this disconnection resulted in a short circuit, which ultimately caused the fuse to blow. the disconnected cable was carefully examined for damage, and continuity testing was performed to verify the integrity of the wiring leading to the magnetic lock supply. the power supply voltage at the connector was also measured to ensure proper output. after that, the wires were securely reconnected to their respective positions within the connector. the blown fuse was replaced with a new one of the appropriate rating. following reassembly, the x-ray machine was powered on. the collimator light illuminated successfully, and the magnetic locking system functioned as expected.

fault_description: the refrigerator was reported as non-functional. the display panel showed persistent door open and high temperature alarms, despite the door being securely closed
action_taken: an initial diagnostic assessment confirmed that the unit was unable to correctly detect the door status. the display continuously indicated a door open alarm, and the internal temperature was rising due to the system s failure to activate cooling under a perceived open-door condition. a detailed inspection was carried out, focusing on the door handle assembly, which incorporates the door sensor wiring.the door handle assembly was dismantled to access the internal wiring. it was found that the sensor wires responsible for communicating door status to the control system were disconnected. the disconnected wires were re-soldered and insulated properly to restore electrical continuity. the door status indicator light changed from inactive to green, confirming accurate detection of the door being closed. the display panel cleared the door open and high temperature alarms. the refrigerator began operating normally, and the internal temperature returned to and maintained the required setpoint for safe blood storage.

fault_description: the ecg machine was reported to produce continuous artifacts in the waveform, which affected accurate interpretation during monitoring. on testing, the device exhibited both baseline wander and emg interference, making the ecg trace unstable and noisy.
action_taken: the ecg cable was tested and found to have damaged insulation on both the main cable and the leads. this damage was allowing external interference to distort the ecg waveform. in addition, there was a significant build-up of conductive gel residue on the leads and electrodes, which was further degrading the quality of the electrode skin interface and contributing to noise artifacts. the damaged sections of the cable and leads were properly insulated to prevent external interference. all leads and electrodes were also thoroughly cleaned to remove conductive gel build-up and restore reliable electrical contact with the patient.after completing these corrective actions, the ecg machine was re-tested. the waveform was found to be stable, free of artifacts, and clear enough for accurate diagnostic interpretation.

action_taken: the ecg machine was reported to produce waveforms with significant artifacts, making clinical interpretation difficult. upon inspection, it was observed that the ecg lead wires were not placed correctly on the patient, leading to improper signal acquisition. in addition, the electrodes had been applied directly to the patient s skin without the use of conductive gel. the absence of conductive gel increased skin-electrode impedance, resulting in unstable contact and noise interference, which resulted in artifacts in the recorded waveform. the ecg leads were correctly placed according to the standard placement by reapplying the electrodes with proper conductive gel to ensure optimal skin contact and reduced impedance. after these adjustments, the ecg waveform was tested again and found to be clear, stable, and free from artifacts.

action_taken: the infant radiant warmer was inspected following a complaint that it was not producing adequate heat. upon evaluation, the device was found to be functioning but was significantly reducing heat output after reaching a certain temperature threshold. the warmer was operating in servo skin mode, in which the device automatically regulates heat output based on the infant s skin temperature relative to a user-defined set point. it was observed that the set temperature had been configured to 32.5 c, which is below the standard target for neonatal care. as a result, the warmer appropriately reduced heating once the infant s skin temperature approached the low set point, leading to perceived underperformance. in accordance to nursing staff, the set temperature was adjusted to 36.5 c, which aligns with typical clinical requirements for neonatal warming. after updating the set point, the warmer responded appropriately by increasing and maintaining adequate heat output.

fault_description: the ecg machine was reported to produce continuous artifacts in the waveform, which hindered accurate interpretation during patient monitoring.
action_taken: a detailed inspection of the ecg cable revealed damaged insulation on both the main cable and the individual leads, along with a breakage in the cable itself. this damage was allowing external electrical interference to distort the ecg waveform. in addition, there was a significant accumulation of conductive gel residue on the leads and electrodes, which was degrading the quality of the electrode skin interface and further contributing to the signal noise. the damaged cable and leads were properly insulated and secured to prevent further interference. all leads and electrodes were thoroughly cleaned to remove the conductive gel build-up. after that, the ecg machine was re-tested. the waveform output was found to be stable, clear, and free of artifacts, confirming the resolution of the issue.

fault_description: the collimator light was non-functional, which affected the ability to accurately visualize and align the x-ray field.
action_taken: the equipment was thoroughly inspected to identify the root cause of the issue. it was found that the fuse supplying power to the lbd was faulty. the defective fuse was replaced with a new, compatible unit. additionally, the power wire connected to the collimator light was found to be disconnected from the connector; this was securely re-soldered to restore proper electrical contact. further inspection revealed that the internal mirror within the collimation assembly was misaligned. the mirror was carefully realigned through the designated adjustment port to ensure the projected light field matched the x-ray exposure area. after completing these corrective actions, the collimator light became functional, and the system was tested to verify that the light field and exposure field were properly aligned. the x-ray machine is now fully functional.

fault_description: reported concern regarding accurate shock energy delivery.
action_taken: a full diagnostic evaluation was conducted to verify the accuracy and reliability of the defibrillator s shock delivery system. the device initially underwent routine self-tests and standard energy delivery checks, all of which passed without errors. further testing was performed using a defibrillator/transcutaneous pacer analyzer to verify manual defibrillation performance. the following tests were carried out as per the service manual: 1. charge/discharge test 2. energy disarming test 3. synchronous defibrillation test 4. ecg performance test during energy delivery verification, multiple energy levels were selected on the defibrillator. for each setting, the device was charged and discharged into the analyzer, and the delivered energy values recorded by the analyzer were compared against the manufacturer-specified tolerances. all measured values were confirmed to be within acceptable limits. the energy disarming function and synchronous shock delivery mode also passed successfully, demonstrating correct operational behavior. based on the module performance tests and analyzer-verified results, the defibrillator is confirmed to deliver accurate shock energy as set, and the unit is functioning within manufacturer specifications.

fault_description: device could not be powered on
action_taken: upon inspection, the warmer did not power on despite being connected to the power supply. the fuse was checked and found to be functional. the main power switch was identified as defective; it was replaced, after which the warmer could be powered on. during further inspection, a burnt connector was identified in the heater supply line. the connector was replaced and re-soldered securely. however, the heater tube still did not heat. the output voltage at the heater terminals on the control board was measured and found to be 0.635 v, which is significantly lower than the required operating voltage. when the heater tube was disconnected, the open-circuit output voltage was 230 v, but when the load (heater tube) was connected, the voltage dropped back to 0.635 v. this indicated that the load was not receiving sufficient current. the heater tube resistance was checked and found to be within the acceptable range, confirming that the heater tube itself was functional. further board-level inspection revealed that the triac output driver (moc3021) had a cold solder joint, preventing proper triggering of the main triac responsible for delivering current to the heater. as a result, the heater was only receiving an unloaded voltage but no actual power under load. the triac driver was re-soldered properly, after which the heater output voltage remained stable at the correct level even with the heater connected. the heater tube subsequently began heating normally. the infant radiant warmer is now fully functional.

fault_description: the centrifuge was unable to start the rotation cycle. the display continuously indicated lid open even when the lid was properly closed, preventing the motor from operating.
action_taken: a detailed inspection was carried out and it was found that the lid/door sensor assembly was faulty. the infrared led and phototransistor inside the sensor had become displaced from their original position due to a broken mounting attachment. as a result, the sensor could not correctly detect the lid status, causing the system to lock out motor activation. the door sensor was disassembled, and the PCB module containing the leds and connector to the control board was realigned and securely repositioned within the sensor housing. after reassembly, the sensor was reinstalled in the centrifuge and its functionality was tested. upon testing, the centrifuge correctly detected the lid as closed, allowing the motor to operate normally. the unit was run at the set rpm and performed without any issues. status: the centrifuge is now fully functional and ready for routine operation.

fault_description: nursing staff reported that the radiant warmer was not providing sufficient heat.
action_taken: upon inspection, the radiant warmer did not power on despite being connected to the mains supply. the power switch was examined and found to be non-functional. the defective switch was replaced. further inspection revealed that the heating tube was not receiving the required supply voltage due to a disconnected wire at the output of the control board responsible for powering the heating element. the loose wire was securely reconnected. after reconnecting the wiring and powering the unit, the display panel failed to turn on. the input voltage to the control board was measured and found to be only 6 v, which is below the required operating voltage. the power supply cable was checked for continuity and found to be intact. on further examination, the fuse was found to be defective. the faulty fuse was replaced. following fuse replacement, the display became functional, and the heating tube operated normally, providing adequate heat output.

fault_description: the autoclave was reported to be non-functional and unable to complete the sterilization cycle.
action_taken: the autoclave was thoroughly inspected to identify the cause of the malfunction. during inspection, it was observed that the emergency safety valve of the boiler was continuously releasing steam. as a result, the required pressure could not be maintained inside the sterilization chamber, leading to interruption of the sterilization process. further investigation revealed that the temperature sensor was improperly positioned, causing incorrect temperature sensing and triggering the safety valve. the temperature sensor was repositioned to the correct level as per operational requirements. after correction, the safety valve stopped releasing steam, and the chamber pressure was maintained within the required range. the autoclave was subsequently tested and confirmed to be operating normally, with the sterilization cycle completing successfully.

fault_description: the compression paddle could not be moved downward.
action_taken: an initial inspection was carried out, during which it was observed that the compression paddle could not be moved down using either the control panel or the footswitch. the footswitch was inspected separately and found to be functioning correctly. it was noted that the paddle could be moved downward using the footswitch only when excessive force was applied. the unit was then partially disassembled, and all internal connections were inspected; no loose or faulty connections were identified. the compression paddle microswitch was checked and found to be non-functional. the microswitch was temporarily bypassed for testing purposes; however, the issue persisted and the paddle still could not be moved down normally. further diagnostics were performed on the load cell system. the excitation voltage supplied to the load cell was measured and found to be within the specified range. however, the load cell was not behaving as expected. the weight displayed on the control panel remained fixed at 17.5 kg and did not fluctuate even when the paddle was moved up or down. the load cell wiring and mounting screws were checked and tightened, but the issue remained unresolved. the load cell was then flipped to rule out orientation-related issues; this also did not resolve the problem. for diagnostic purposes, the signal wire to the load cell was temporarily shorted. under this condition, the compression paddle could be moved up and down smoothly using both the footswitch and the control panel; however, the displayed weight remained fixed at 5 kg. after consultation with the radiology staff, it was confirmed that exposure parameters are selected based on breast size rather than compression weight. as a temporary measure, the system was operated with the displayed weight fixed at 5 kg, allowing normal paddle movement and the microswitch has been replaced as well. conclusion / recommendation: preliminary findings indicate that the load cell is faulty and not providing accurate weight feedback to the system. replacement of the load cell is recommended. after replacement, further evaluation will be required to determine whether any additional components are contributing to the issue.

fault_description: abnormal bellows performance and mismatch between displayed tidal volume and actual bellows movement.
action_taken: the anesthesia machine was inspected and ventilation was initiated for functional evaluation. it was observed that the tidal volume displayed on the monitor did not correspond with the physical movement of the bellows, indicating a ventilation measurement or mechanical issue. on further inspection, moisture accumulation was found inside the flow sensor. the flow sensor was cleaned and dried thoroughly. additionally, the bellows assembly was examined and found that the valve within the bellows mechanism had been displaced, preventing proper seating and normal operation. the valve and bellows were correctly repositioned and secured. following reassembly, a leak test was performed to assess the integrity of the breathing system. outcome: the leak test was successfully passed. post-repair functional testing confirmed that the tidal volume displayed on the monitor accurately matched the bellows movement. the anesthesia machine is now functioning normally and is safe for clinical use.

fault_description: error during the warm-up process; analyzer failed to complete initialization.
action_taken: the biochemistry analyzer was inspected and powered on for observation. during the warm-up sequence, the machine displayed an error message and failed to complete the warm-up process. further inspection revealed that the sample arm was stuck in a fixed position, preventing normal initialization. the device was safely disassembled to access the sample arm assembly. the position-sensing sensor responsible for detecting the sample arm movement was inspected and found to have residue buildup, which was obstructing proper sensor detection. the sensor area was cleaned thoroughly, and accumulated dust within the assembly was removed using a blower. after cleaning, the sample arm was manually moved up and down several times to ensure free and smooth movement and proper sensor response. outcome: the device was reassembled and powered on. the analyzer completed the warm-up process successfully without displaying any error messages. normal movement of the sample arm was confirmed, and the device is now functioning properly and ready for use.

fault_description: the x-ray tube support arm could not be moved up or down and could not be locked in position.
action_taken: the portable x-ray unit was inspected with particular attention to the arm movement and locking mechanism. during inspection, it was found that the locking mechanism was not functioning due to displacement of the locking component and the associated spring. further examination revealed that the fixing screw responsible for securing the locking mechanism had lost its threads and could no longer be tightened properly, resulting in failure of the locking system. as an interim corrective measure, a suitable alternative screw along with a washer was installed to securely fasten the locking mechanism. this substitution was carried out with assistance from the oxygen department. after the repair, the arm movement was restored. the arm could be smoothly moved up and down and could be securely locked at the desired position. the unit is currently functioning normally.

fault_description: intermittent exposure failure with a filament interlock error; further exposures could not be performed after a single exposure.
action_taken: the mammography unit was inspected following the reported exposure issue. during testing, it was observed that after performing one exposure, the system displayed a filament interlock error, and subsequent exposures were inhibited. additionally, the parameters on the control panel could not be adjusted once the error occurred. since filament interlock errors commonly arise due to loose or improper electrical connections, a thorough inspection of the system connections was carried out. the connections at the tube head and the associated cables leading to the high-voltage (hv) tank were checked and found to be secure. all internal connections within the control panel were also inspected and confirmed to be intact. further investigation revealed that an exposure was being initiated even when only the ready button on the hand switch was pressed, without fully engaging the exposure switch. to isolate the source of the issue, the hand switch was disconnected and exposures were performed using the control panel controls. under this condition, the filament interlock error did not recur, and multiple exposures were successfully performed. the hand switch was then disassembled for detailed inspection. a disconnected wire was found in the connector section of the hand switch, which was causing improper signal transmission and unintended exposure initiation. the wire was securely reconnected, and the hand switch was reassembled. after repair, the hand switch functionality was tested and confirmed to be normal. the system was operated with the hand switch connected, and multiple exposures were performed without any recurrence of the filament interlock error. final status the hand switch was restored to proper working condition. the mammography unit is now functioning normally, and exposures can be performed reliably without interlock errors.

action_taken: the patient monitor was inspected to identify the cause of the reported issue. during initial observation, it was confirmed that the spo₂ reading was not displayed on the monitor. on further inspection, it was found that the spo₂ module had been accidentally deactivated, which interrupted the display and processing of the spo₂ signal. the spo₂ module was reactivated, and the system was checked again. after activating the module, the spo₂ probe was inspected for proper functionality. it was observed that the red led light in the spo₂ probe was not illuminating, indicating a probe malfunction. to rule out monitor-side issues, the probe was cross-checked using another compatible spo₂ probe, with which the monitor displayed normal spo₂ readings.this confirmed that the issue was isolated to the original spo₂ probe. final status: the patient monitor is functioning correctly, and the spo₂ module is operational. however, the spo₂ probe is faulty and requires replacement.

fault_description: no heat output from the radiant warmer.
action_taken: the device was inspected following the complaint of no heat generation. the output voltage at the control board was measured and found to be 230 v, indicating that the power supply to the heater tube was normal. however, despite the presence of the correct voltage, the heater tube was not producing heat. further inspection of the heater circuit revealed a discontinuity in the wiring. upon tracing the circuit, the fuse was found to be defective (blown), which was interrupting the power supply to the heater tube. the defective fuse was replaced with a new one of the correct rating, and the disconnected/loose wiring was properly reconnected and secured. after replacement and reconnection, the unit was powered on and tested. the heater tube started heating normally, and the warmer function was restored.

fault_description: the unit was not delivering consistent output in both cut and coag modes.
action_taken: the electrosurgical unit was inspected after the user reported inconsistent output. initial testing confirmed that both cut and coagulation modes were not producing stable output. the handpiece was replaced to rule out accessory-related issues; however, the problem persisted. the patient plate indicator showed a continuous red light, which indicates an improper or failed patient plate connection. the patient plate and its cable were tested for continuity, and the signal path from the plate connector to the main board was also checked. both the patient plate and the wiring were found to be functional. further troubleshooting revealed that there was no dc voltage output from the power supply section. the board was inspected, and it was found that the fuse was defective. in addition, multiple components on the board were found to be faulty, including the pulse wave modulator, capacitor, and diode. after resolving the issue, the unit was powered on and re-tested. the patient plate red indicator turned off, confirming a secure and proper patient plate connection. functional testing was performed again. at this stage, the coagulation mode was working properly, but the cut mode was still not producing output. on further inspection, multiple desoldered wire connections were found inside the unit. these connections were properly re-soldered and secured. after completing all repairs and re-soldering the loose connections, the unit was tested again. both cut and coagulation modes were found to be working properly and producing consistent output. status: the unit is fully functional and operating normally.

fault_description: reported non-functional refrigerator with door open alarm and incorrect door status indication.

fault_description: preventive maintenance of the endoscopy system was carried out by the supplier as per the recommended maintenance protocol.
action_taken: the functionality of the colonoscope was tested and found to be operating as expected. leakage tests were performed on all three scopes colonoscope, gastroscope, and bronchoscope and no leakage was detected in any of the scopes. the suction knob, which had been previously reported as non-functional, was repaired by the supplier. its functionality was tested after repair and found to be satisfactory. issue identified: during testing of the bronchoscope, multiple spots were observed on the display screen. initial inspection suggested surface contamination; therefore, the camera was cleaned, which temporarily reduced the appearance of the spots. however, after disconnecting and reconnecting the scope and allowing some time to pass, the spots reappeared. further evaluation confirmed that the spots were due to fungal growth, caused by moisture accumulation and improper storage of the scope. the issue was not related to residual debris. corrective action and recommendation: the supplier advised that the bronchoscope should be stored in a hanging position rather than kept inside a storage box to prevent moisture retention and fungal growth. current status: the bronchoscope has been taken by the supplier for further rectification. an estimated time of up to two weeks has been provided for resolution of the issue.

action_taken: three patient monitors (serial nos.: picu003, picu008, and picu009) were reported to have issues with nibp measurement. each unit was inspected and tested individually. during inspection, it was observed that the monitors continuously inflated the nibp cuff and failed to detect the maximum inflation pressure, resulting in unsuccessful or inaccurate nibp readings. the nibp cables and connectors were cross-checked by interchanging them among the three monitors and were found to be fully functional. the nibp modules of all three monitors were also tested and confirmed to be operating. further investigation identified air leakage in the nibp cuffs as the root cause of the issue. due to the leakage, the system was unable to maintain adequate pressure during measurement. conclusion / recommendation: the nibp cuffs of all three monitors are defective and must be replaced to
